# Phase II Open-label Non-randomized Multicenter Clinical Trial of Trametinib for Dogs With Histiocytic Sarcoma

The University of Florida College of Veterinary Medicine is currently recruiting dogs diagnosed with Histiocytic Sarcoma for a clinical research trial.

Enrollment Criteria: Currently Enrolling

  * Inclusion Criteria: Your dog has been diagnosed with Histiocytic Sarcoma
  * Treatment: Prior to treatment with the study drug (trametinib), a tumor biopsy, and a blood sample (less than one ounce) will be collected. A tumor biopsy will be taken only when tumors are accessible, via a small incision through the skin, and collection of a small piece of tumor tissue, with the patient under sedation. Enrolled dogs will have a physical examination, laboratory analysis, blood pressure measurement, and diagnostic imaging (x-rays and ultrasound). Trametinib will be given by mouth, once daily, as long as your dog is responding to treatment

  * Cost: This study will cover the costs of the Trametinib medication, recheck physical examination fees, collection of blood and tumor samples for investigation, and routine laboratory tests/diagnostic imaging (thoracic radiographs and abdominal ultrasound) at scheduled recheck study visits.
  * Contact: Please complete the Study Interest Form for more information.
  * PI: Dr. Marilia Takada and Dr. Paulo Vilar Saavedra

Background: The purpose of this research is to investigate a new anti-cancer drug, trametinib, that specifically ‘targets’ growth signals found in cancer cells from companion (pet) dogs. This study will determine the anti-tumor efficacy of trametinib in dogs with histiocytic sarcoma. We will measure and document how much the cancer shrinks upon treatment, and how the drug helps improve the patients’ outcome and life expectancy. Additionally, the study will test whether markers in the genes within the tumor can predict the response from treatment, which in the future can help select those dogs that are more likely to respond positively to treatment. Finally, in a simple blood test we will determine whether effective drug levels are present in the patient.

# SBRT for Canine Lung Tumor Study

  * Recruiting
  * Dog
  * Oncology

Primary pulmonary carcinomas in dogs are most commonly treated with surgery, which can result in survival times of approximately one year. Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a highly precise form of radiation therapy that delivers high doses of radiation directly to a tumor while minimizing exposure to surrounding normal tissues. The purpose of this study is to evaluate dogs with primary pulmonary carcinoma treated using a standardized SBRT protocol across institutions participating in the Veterinary Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (VRTOG).

## Inclusion Criteria

Dogs are eligible for enrollment if they meet all of the following criteria:

  * Cytologic or histopathologic diagnosis of a single primary pulmonary carcinoma.
  * Primary lung tumor measuring greater than 1 cm in its shortest diameter.
  * No previous treatment for the lung tumor.
  * No diagnosis of another malignant tumor outside the lungs within 30 days before enrollment.
  * Complete blood count, serum biochemistry panel, and abdominal ultrasound performed within 30 days before enrollment.
  * Considered an appropriate candidate for stereotactic radiation therapy by the attending veterinary oncologist or radiation oncologist.
  * Dogs with a previous non-carcinoma malignancy may be enrolled if that tumor type is associated with an expected median survival time greater than one year and the dog is considered to be in clinical remission at enrollment.

## Exclusion Criteria

Dogs will not be enrolled if any of the following are present:

  * Multiple pulmonary nodules consistent with metastatic disease.
  * Evidence of regional lymph node metastasis.
  * Pulmonary carcinomatosis.
  * Significant concurrent disease expected to limit survival to less than one year.
  * Medical conditions that preclude safe anesthesia or radiation treatment.

## Client Benefits

While your dog is enrolled in the study, the study will contribute up to $4,000 toward the costs of anesthesia, radiation treatment planning, and radiation therapy. Up to $1,000 may also be available for follow-up thoracic radiographs after treatment.

Owners are responsible for the costs of pre-enrollment bloodwork, CT imaging required for radiation planning, and confirmation of the tumor diagnosis.

Owners are also responsible for costs related to hospitalization if complications occur.

## Sample or Data Requirements

If your dog participates in this study, they will receive SBRT while under general anesthesia.

Prior to radiation therapy, a CT scan will be performed to create the radiation treatment plan. Thoracic radiographs (chest X-rays) will also be obtained before treatment to establish a baseline. Follow-up radiographs will be performed approximately 2 weeks, 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, and then every 3 months to evaluate treatment response until your dog leaves the study.

## Contact Information

For questions regarding the clinical trial, please email clinicaltrials@tufts.edu.

## 

### Pet Eligibility Questionnaire

If you believe that your pet may be eligible for this study, please complete our prescreening questionnaire for owners.

### Referring Physician Questionnaire

If you believe you have a patient who is eligible for this clinical trial study or you would like additional information from the Clinical Trials Office, complete a referring physician questionnaire.

### 招募犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤臨床試驗

#### 招募犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤臨床試驗

台北長青動物醫院總院正在招募罹患黑色素瘤(melanoma)或骨肉瘤(oesteosarcoma)的狗參與臨床試驗！

此次的試驗是將IL15透過噴霧治療形式進行治療。IL15是一種細胞激素，具有促進免疫與抑制腫瘤生長的效果。

有許多人類腫瘤臨床試驗顯示IL-15具有治療腫瘤的潛力，此種藥物最近也被應用在狗的黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤，初步結果指出IL-15對這類患犬同樣具有治療效益。

試驗目的在於進一步驗證IL15 對於犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤長期控制的效果。

關於這個試驗的重點Q&A

1.這項治療的原理是什麼？IL-15是一種細胞激素，能夠刺激自身的免疫細胞（NK細胞、T細胞）對抗腫瘤的生長和轉移。

2.參加試驗的狗須符合哪些條件a.經細胞學或組織病理學確診罹患黑色素瘤或骨肉瘤。b.患犬品種、年齡、體重、性別不限。c.肺部轉移病灶直徑需大於1.0公分。d.患犬沒有出現危及生命的腫瘤相關症狀。e.目前沒有使用類固醇或其他免疫抑制劑。f. 飼主須能配合每周回診治療追蹤，療程約10~12週。

3.治療過程是如何進行？IL15藥劑以皮下注射方式給藥。若有肺部腫瘤轉移則會將藥劑放置在噴霧機內，患犬在清醒的狀態下佩戴呼吸面罩，含有藥劑的噴霧會隨著呼吸進入狗的肺部。

4.多久需回診一次？每週治療一次，共八次治療。治療結束後兩週需回診追蹤療效。

5.治療過程中需要進行哪些檢驗？治療前需進行血檢、尿檢、X光或電腦斷層確認腫瘤狀態。治療當日需抽血檢查。療程結束後會再次進行血檢、尿檢、X光或電腦斷層評估效果。

6.參加這項試驗的狗可能有什麼副作用？初步的研究顯示腫瘤患犬使用IL15可能發生的副作用為疲倦、嗜睡、肝指數上升、下痢、呼吸加快等，大多數情況下這類副作用並不會危及生命，可自行緩解。

7.參加這項試驗對我的狗有什麼好處？先前的臨床試驗顯示IL15可以讓部分患犬的腫瘤縮小或消失，參加此次試驗的狗可能達到類似的效果。相較於傳統的血管注射化療，副作用的發生機率與嚴重程度較低。

8.參加試驗需要費用嗎？此次試驗的IL15藥劑不收費，治療過程中所需的檢查及輔助用藥費用需由飼主自行負擔。

此試驗通過獸醫內科醫學會動物試驗研究倫理委員會審核，有意願參加試驗請電話預約長青動物醫院總院腫瘤門診。預約時請告訴櫃檯人員要參加 〝IL15臨床試驗〞，或填寫以下表單，醫院人員會去電或email與您聯絡安排門診時間。

電話：02-23369908 地址：台北市萬華區廣州街78號

## Kv9 Pilot Study

Purpose of study: 

To assess efficacy and safety of Kv9 across a range of solid tumours. 

Eligible tumour types: 

  * Soft tissue sarcomas 

  * Mast cell tumours 

  * Mammary gland tumours

  * Melanomas 

  * Anal gland tumours 

  * Squamous cell carcinomas 

  * Other tumours may be considered 

Primary eligibility criteria*: ​

  * Tumour type diagnosed by fine needle aspirate or biopsy by a registered veterinary pathologist 

  * ​Tumour smaller than 5cm 

  * Not receiving immune modulatory drugs

    * It is acceptable to be taking/receiving including apoquel, cytopoint, beranza or a recent vaccination 

  * No wounds on the surface of soft tissue sarcoma tumours

    * Other tumour types will be a case by case basis ​

*See referral form for complete criteria ​

Study protocol: 

  1. Primary veterinarian to send through referral for assessment by Kode Veterinary Sciences (KVS). 

  2. Additional testing completed as required. 

  3. Atleast two treatment appointments to receive Kv9 at treatment centres.

  4. A minimum of 9 revisits at primary care veterinarian or treatment centres over 2 years. 

Owner responsibilities: 

  * You are responsible to schedule and attend all required visits  ​

  * You are responsible for the initial costs to diagnose your dogs tumour, and any other tests recommended by your veterinarian  

  * You are responsible to closely monitor your pet for any changes and update the clinical study team in a timely manner 

Financial support: 

  * There is no cost to participate in the clinical study. KVS will cover the cost of treatment and monitoring appointments, and provide the Kv9 treatment free of charge. 

  * KVS will provide support to any participant experiencing adverse events during their time in the trial. If the event is suspected to be related to the Kv9 treatment, KVS will provide financial support, unless agreed to be excluded in the consent form.

# Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) for lung metastases

  * Recruiting
  * Dog
  * Oncology

This study will evaluate whether a single, highly focused dose of radiation can safely treat cancer that has spread to the lungs in dogs. Our radiation treatment is administered externally by delivering high-energy x-rays directly to the tumor so there is no risk of radiation exposure for people in contact with pets receiving this type of therapy. We will assess how practical the treatment is, including treatment planning, managing breathing during radiation for prolonged periods of time, radiation delivery, and the time dogs need to be under anesthesia. The study will also monitor dogs for short- and long-term side effects and evaluate how well the treated tumors respond. Investigators will track how long the treated tumors remain under control and how long the dogs remain free from further cancer progression. The goal is to determine whether this single radiation treatment can safely and effectively control cancerous spread to the lungs.

## Inclusion Criteria

Dogs are eligible for enrollment if they meet all of the following criteria:

  * Confirmed malignancy: Cytologic or histopathologic confirmation of a malignant tumor (e.g., carcinoma, sarcoma, or melanoma) with pulmonary nodules consistent with metastasis to the lungs.
  * Limited and progressive pulmonary metastases: Presence of 2–10 pulmonary nodules consistent with oligometastatic disease. Disease progression must be documented on thoracic radiographs or CT (Computed Tomography) imaging over at least 6–8 weeks, defined as either a ≥20% increase in lesion size or the development of new pulmonary lesions, according to VCOG v1.0 criteria.
  * Control of primary and other metastatic disease: The primary tumor and any confirmed regional lymph node metastases must have been adequately controlled with definitive-intent surgery and/or radiation therapy. Any confirmed metastatic disease outside the lungs must also be adequately controlled with appropriate local and/or systemic therapy.
  * Expected survival: An estimated survival time of at least 3 months, as determined by the attending veterinary oncologist.
  * Recent thoracic imaging: Three-view thoracic radiographs, accompanied by a radiology report, obtained within 1 month before enrollment.
  * SABR candidacy and technical feasibility: The attending veterinary radiation oncologist must determine that the dog is an appropriate candidate for stereotactic ablative radiation therapy (SABR). The radiation oncologist must determine that all progressive pulmonary lesions measuring ≥5 mm can be safely and technically treated, while meeting the study-defined lung dose constraint.
  * Adequate overall health: Acceptable clinical status, including an ECOG (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group) performance status <2, adequate blood cell counts and organ function, and the ability to safely undergo general anesthesia. A complete blood count and serum biochemistry panel must be obtained within 30 days before anesthesia.
  * Owner consent: Written informed owner consent must be obtained before enrollment.

## Sample or Data Requirements

If your dog participates in this study, they will receive a single, highly targeted dose of radiation therapy while under general anesthesia. Before treatment, a CT scan (3D imaging technique) will be performed to develop a personalized radiation treatment plan. A follow-up examination will be performed approximately one (1) month after treatment to assess for any side effects. A final follow-up examination and CT scan, performed under heavy sedation or anesthesia, will be performed approximately 2–3 months after radiation therapy to evaluate the tumor’s response to treatment. If your pet develops coughing, difficulty breathing, or other respiratory concerns during the study period, a recheck examination and chest X-rays will be recommended.

## Contact Information

For questions regarding the clinical trial, please email clinicaltrials@tufts.edu.

### Referring Physician Questionnaire

If you believe you have a patient who is eligible for this clinical trial study or you would like additional information from the Clinical Trials Office, complete a referring physician questionnaire.

L9: # Register your interest in our dog cancer trial
L10: 
L11: We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

L15: Why we are running this trial
L16: ## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.
L17: 
L18: 【9†Image: Rosie】
L19: 
L20: Rosie
L21: 
L22: The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.
L23: 
L24: It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.
L25: Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.

L112: Although clinical trial enrollment may not be the best option for all patients, in many cases, clinical trial participation provides the opportunity to receive novel, cutting-edge therapies free of charge or at a reduced cost and may facilitate treatment of pets where it would not otherwise be possible due to financial constraints or lack of other therapy options. Criteria for enrollment are outlined for each tumor type below.
L114: Current Trials and Studies
L115: 
L116: Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BI705564) for Canine B‑Cell Lymphoma
L117: 
L118: The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling dogs in a clinical trial evaluating an investigational oral Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor—BI705564—for the treatment of newly diagnosed B‑cell lymphoma. This exploratory, multicenter field study aims to assess both efficacy and safety of BTK inhibition in canine patients.
L119: 
L120: Eligibility includes:
L121:   * Dogs >1 year old and 10–50 kg in body weight
L122:   * Naïve, untreated B‑cell lymphoma confirmed by cytology or histology with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry)
L123:   * At least two peripheral lymph nodes ≥2 cm in longest diameter
L124:   * WHO stage II, III, or IV B‑cell lymphoma
L125:   * Adequate organ function on bloodwork and urinalysis
L126:   * Performance score of 0–1 (normal to mildly decreased activity) and life expectancy ≥1 month
L127:   * Owner consent
L128: 
L129: Key exclusions:
L130:   * T‑cell lymphoma or involvement of skin, GI tract, or nervous system
L131:   * Internal‑only disease (mediastinum, liver, spleen) without peripheral lymph node enlargement
L132:   * Prior lymphoma treatment (chemotherapy, Tanovea, Laverdia, radiation) or long‑term corticosteroids (>2 weeks)
L133:   * Hypercalcemia, MDR1 deficiency, pregnancy/lactation, or concurrent trial enrollment
L134: 
L135: Study overview:
L136: Dogs will receive oral BI705564 once daily for 3 months (84 days) at 5 mg/kg, with possible dose escalation to 10 mg/kg in certain cases depending on early target occupancy results.
L137: 
L138: The study includes scheduled evaluations such as:
L139: 
L140:   * Physical examinations and lymph node measurements
L141:   * Quality‑of‑life assessments
L142:   * Bloodwork (CBC, chemistry, lymphoma testing)
L143:   * Lymph node aspirates for target occupancy evaluation
L144:   * Thoracic radiographs and abdominal ultrasound at screening
L145: Follow‑up continues regularly throughout the 12‑week treatment period.
L146: 
L147: Potential benefits:
L148: 
L149:   * Access to a novel investigational BTK inhibitor designed to target B‑cell lymphoma
L150:   * All study‑related diagnostics, monitoring, and investigational drug costs are covered
L151:   * Opportunity to contribute to advancement of veterinary oncology and comparative cancer therapeutics
L152: 
L153: Potential risks:
L154:   * Possible drug‑related side effects (as with any investigational therapy)
L155:   * Risks associated with repeated lymph node aspirates, blood draws, and imaging procedures
L156:   * Dogs may be withdrawn if adverse events occur or if continued participation is not in the animal’s best interest
L157: 
L158: Owner commitment:
L159: 
L160: Owners must agree to:
L161:   * Bring their dog for all required study visits over 12 weeks
L162:   * Administer oral medication daily as directed
L163:   * Allow required diagnostic sampling (bloodwork, lymph node aspirates, imaging)
L164:   * Participate in quality‑of‑life assessments
L165: 
L166: Dogs may be withdrawn at any time. If a dog passes away during the study, postmortem evaluation is requested to improve understanding of treatment effects.
L167: 
L168: Contact
L169: For more information on this study please contact:
L170: 📧 cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu
L171: Please include the subject line: BI705564 BTK Inhibitor Trial

L173: COTC033: Repurposing Vaccine Immunity to Treat Cancers
L174: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of a new immunotherapy, the Vaccine Peptide Library (VPL), when given to dogs with cancer. Studies in dogs with cancer will complement current human trials designed to test new doses and effects of this agent.
L175: 
L176: Criteria:
L177:   * Body weight between 15 and 60 kg
L178:   * Tumor biopsy or cytology to confirm diagnosis
L179:   * Solid tumor measuring 2 to 8 cm
L180:   * No mast cell tumors, cutaneous hemangiosarcomas, thyroid carcinomas, or lymphomas
L181:   * Must not have received ANY prior experimental therapy
L182:   * No concurrent chemotherapy or radiation therapy – 2 week washout period required
L183:   * No concurrent immunomodulatory therapy (including Apoquel or Cytopoint) – 6 week washout period required
L184:   * No concurrent corticosteroids – 1 week washout period required
L185:   * No hypercalcemia causing illness
L186:   * No significant co-morbid illness, which includes, but is not limited to: pulmonary metastatic disease, renal or hepatic failure, history of congestive heart failure or clinical coagulopathy, autoimmune disorders, or uncontrolled endocrinopathies
L187: Benefit:
L188: 
L189:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks covered by study, include initial staging or adverse side effects.
L190:   * This trial is being conducted concurrently with human trials.
L191:   * Contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L192:   * At the conclusion of the study, there will be a $1000 monetary gift provided towards additional treatment for your pet’s cancer.
L193: 
L194: To Participate:
L195:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L196:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L197:   * Participation will require a total of up to 13 weekly visits.
L198: 
L199: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【70†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L200: Feline GI Lymphoma Radiation + Chemotherapy
L201: 
L202: The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of whole abdomen radiation therapy (WART) followed by a chemotherapy protocol (COP/Dox) in cats with spontaneous large cell GI lymphoma.  This study will seek to better understand the effects of radiation therapy prior to receiving chemotherapy for this common feline cancer.
L203: 
L204: Criteria:
L205:   * Feline patients with high grade lymphoma in the GI tract
L206:   * Patients must have cytologically or histopathologically confirmed lymphoma
L207:   * Patients must not have been previously treated with chemotherapy
L208:   * Patients cannot be FeLV or FIV positive or have severe systemic disease that would place them at higher risk with general anesthesia.
L209:   * Patients CANNOT have evidence of lymphoma outside of the abdomen.
L210:   * Eligibility is at the discretion of the investigator.
L211: 
L212: Benefit:
L213:   * The cost of the radiation portion of care (WART) will be covered by the study.
L214:   * Your pet will contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L215:   * Patient will receive $1,000 stipend for use at the VHC after completion of radiation therapy
L216: 
L217: To Participate:
L218:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their cat to and from the treatment center in Columbia, Missouri, for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L219:   * A full screening including a CBC (complete blood count), serum biochemistry panel, urinalysis, thoracic radiographs (x-rays), and abdominal ultrasound will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L220:   * Participation will require pets to come to our clinic weekly for a minimum of eight weeks and then every 3 weeks for 5 additional visits, with radiation administered the first week only.
L221: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.

L223: Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Primary Pulmonary Carcinoma in Dogs
L224: 
L225: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of Gilvetmab, an anti-PD1 monoclonal antibody, as a treatment for canine pulmonary carcinoma. Similar treatments have been shown to improve survival in human lung cancer patients.
L226: Criteria:
L227: 
L228:   * Dogs with gross disease and those with microscopic disease
L229:   * No immune-mediated disease or other severe comorbidities
L230:   * No concurrent use of steroids or other immunosuppressive drugs
L231: 
L232: Study Involvement:
L233: 
L234:   * Gilvetmab is given as a slow infusion every two weeks for up to 10 doses.
L235:   * CBC, chemistry, and urinalysis are performed every 4 weeks.
L236:   * Chest x-rays are performed every 8 weeks.
L237: 
L238: Benefit:
L239:   * The study covers the cost of Gilvetmab treatment (ranges from $540 – $1350 per treatment, depending on patient size).
L240:   * Owner is responsive for recheck exams, bloodwork, and x-rays.

L242: To Participate:

L244:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L245:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L246:   * Participation will require a total of up to 10 biweekly visits.
L247: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【71†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】

L249: LEAH xCAR-T: Canine B-Cell Lymphoma
L250: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lymphodepleting chemotherapy and xenogenic CAR-T cell therapy in dogs with spontaneous CD20+ lymphoma. CAR-T cells are lymphocytes (immune cells) that have had a series of genes added to them that make them professional killers of any cell carrying the target molecule.
L251: This study will seek to better understand the effects of the CAR-T cells on the tumor as well as the dog’s immune system.
L252: Criteria:
L253: 
L254:   * Canine patients weighing over 10kg
L255: 
L256:   * Patients with naive (newly diagnosed) and relapsed (pre-treated) Large Cell B-Cell lymphoma.
L257: 
L258:   * Must be feeling clinically WELL at home.
L259: 
L260:   * Must meet bloodwork requirements and have no evidence of primary gastrointestinal or lung involvement; eligibility is at the discretion of the investigator.
L261:   * Patients CANNOT be receiving immunomodulatory drugs (Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, azathioprine).
L262:   * Patients must be off prednisone for a minimum of 72 hours prior to CAR-T therapy.
L263: 
L264: Benefit:
L265: 
L266:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks are covered by study, including initial staging; up to $4,000 allotted for possible adverse events; $2,000 stipend for additional/future treatment at the VHC upon completion
L267: 
L268:   * You pet will contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L269: To Participate:
L270: 
L271:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, Missouri, for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L272: 
L273:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L274: 
L275:   * Participation will require pets to come to our clinic for a minimum of seven visits over the first 21 days of the study, with future longer-term follow up appointments required, and/or until progression or relapse.
L276: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.

L278: Thyroid Sodium Iodide Symporter
L279: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial to assess whether using special stains for the sodium iodide symporter can allow us to identify tumors that are taking up iodine after a thyroid tumor has been removed. This would limit the need for expensive thyroid scans before surgery and increase the number of dogs that could be considered for additional treatment if their thyroid cancer is aggressive.
L280: 
L281: Criteria:
L282:   * Dogs with presumed thyroid carcinoma considered likely candidates for thyroidectomy
L283:   * Patients who have received neoadjuvant radiation (external beam or I-131) or chemotherapy, exogenous iodine supplementation are not eligible.
L284: 
L285: Benefit:
L286:   * The pre-operative thyroid scan would allow radioactive iodine therapy to be considered as an option following surgery, if there were concerns that your dog’s thyroid tumor was more aggressive than usual.
L287:   * After enrollment, the study will contribute $1,500 to cover associated clinical costs. This includes coverage of costs associated with the pre-operative thyroid scan, including sedation and hospital care (approximately ($1,055).

L163: #### Whole-exome sequencing
L164: 
L165: We compare DNA from the tumour biopsy against a matched blood sample. Only mutations present in the tumour, absent from healthy tissue, are candidate targets. Everything else is filtered out from the start.
L166: 
L167: 【20†Image】
L168: #### Neoantigen prioritisation
L169: 
L170: Our pipeline runs binding affinity predictions and immunogenicity scoring across all somatic mutations, using models trained on canine biology. The highest-confidence candidates are ranked and surfaced for your review before any manufacturing begins.
L171: 
L172: 【21†Image】
L173: #### mRNA delivery
L174: 
L175: Selected neoantigens are encoded into a codon-optimised mRNA sequence built for canine cells. When administered, the patient's cells briefly display cancer-specific markers, activating a targeted T-cell response directed only at tumour cells.
